item.title: Note 13
item.description:
Notes No. 13
Past the optimum, more risk per trade means slower growth. Growth peaks at 25% risked and is zero at 50%.
Consider a system that wins half its trades, with each win twice the size of each loss, and a fixed fraction of capital risked on every trade. The long-run compound growth rate is 0.5 × ln(1 + 2f) + 0.5 × ln(1 − f), where f is the fraction risked. It peaks at 25%, the Kelly fraction for this edge, falls back to zero at 50%, and is negative beyond that, so capital shrinks over time despite the positive expectancy. Risking 12.5% or 37.5% gives exactly the same growth rate, but the larger size carries far deeper drawdowns.
Notes from my trading. Not investment advice.
